modes.name: do_not_cite_policy_id
modes.definition: The reply contains a cw-* or store-* policy identifier and the caller's role is shopper or merchant.
modes.requirement_source: none exists — needs a spec revision. RESP-1 currently requires citing the identifier for every policy claim, so   this mode contradicts the spec as written.
modes.boundary: vs. #4: this is about the identifier string being visible, not about whether the policy claim was correct. A reply that cites the right policy with the wrong content is not this mode.

modes.name: internal_identifier_volunteered
modes.definition: The reply states an order number, ticket id, or store id that the user did not supply in the conversation.
modes.requirement_source: RESP-4 covers inaccessible data only; these ids belong to the caller, so nothing currently forbids showing them.
modes.boundary: vs. #1: policy identifiers are documentation references; these are record identifiers. The "did the user supply it?" test is what separates a positive from a close negative here, and it doesn't apply to #1.

modes.name: escalation_without_basis
modes.definition: The reply escalates or offers to escalate to a human when none of ESC-1 to ESC-4 applies (no above-threshold refund, no account change, no dispute, no genuine policy ambiguity).
modes.requirement_source: needs a spec revision. ESC-1 to ESC-4 say when escalation is required, never when it's forbidden.
modes.boundary: This covers a handoff the agent could perform but shouldn't; #4 covers a capability the agent claims but doesn't have.

modes.name: unsupported_capability_or_speculation
modes.definition: The reply offers an action, ability, or explanation that no tool or policy document supports — inventing a capability, or speculating about how Cartwheel works.
modes.requirement_source: RESP-3 ("state when required information is missing or inconsistent, rather than inventing a value"), with SCOPE-1 for offers outside the agent's abilities.
modes.boundary: escalation is a real capability being offered in the wrong situation; this is a capability that doesn't exist at all.
